To the long list of women who are holding important war posts another name must be added, that of Miss Maria Dahn, of New York City. Despite her youth she is now filling a position for the Navy Department that requires a high degree of technical skill. Miss Dahn is a finger print expert in the bureau of identifications and her work is very important in keeping track of the men serving in every branch of the Navy.

TRAINING THE NEWLAI ARMY
The young women whose patience has moved them to become farm
hands are seen a training school near Theydon Bois Essex. They
work here a month until they acquire a good serviceable
knowledge of the duties required $2000 of them and are then
drafted elsewhere. Special attention is devoted to milking as
clumsy fingers call easily spoil a milch cow worth £50 now.

Now in New York on a tour of the continent, 16 year old Birdie Reeve, of St Louis, who can typewrite at the rate of 250 words a minute and, according to her father, held as many as 20 keys a second when going at top speed, with accuracy. But that's not all. She knows--really knows, spelling, pronunciation, and meaning--sixty-four thousand (64,000) words. And, although she left school at 12 to concentrate on becoming the world's best typist, she has managed to read all of Dickens and Thackeray. And that, too, is rather unusual in these days when sophisticated sixteen sneers at 'em as snuffy, formal, and cut-of-date. & 7/21/23

MRS. STEWART SELECTED AS PRIVATE SECRETARY TO CABINET MEMBER.
First woman to act in such capacity proves invaluable to Mr. Redfield.
Miss Agatha Olsen Stewart of Port Richmond, S.W. has the honor and the distinction of being the first woman to act in the capacity of a private secretary to a cabinet member.

When Mr. Redfield was elected to congress she went to Washington as his confidential clerk. After Mr. Redfield's appointment to Pres. Wilson's cabinet as secretary of the Department of Commerce he took Miss Steward along to act as his private secretary, which position she is now filling with great satisfaction.

The American Branch of Nursing, International who have been holding their Annual Congress in Paris, visited the devastated areas of Scissons and Cocy le Chateau on Friday 16th. The photo shows Major Julia Stinson of the United States Army (with furs) talking to some of the children whom the Americans have succoured.
